items.text: Adults 21 and over (visitors included) may possess up to 2.5 ounces of cannabis, of which no more than 15 g concentrate. Public consumption is banned, property owners can prohibit use, and cannabis can't be taken across state lines.

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Isle Royale National Park
layers.process: Isle Royale is reached by ferry or seaplane (park season 16 April to 31 October). Daily entrance fee US$7 per person aged 16 and over (about A$9.90) for each calendar day in the park; it is cashless. Every overnight party of 1 to 6 people needs a small-party permit: no extra fee, issued free by a ranger on the ferry or on arrival (seaplane arrivals self-permit), and campsites are first come, first served. Groups of 7 or more need a group camping permit with advance reservation. Display the permit on the pack or tent and return it before leaving the island. The US$60 Season Pass is for US citizens or residents. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.

laws.rule: Michigan state parks and recreation areas: drones must not be flown within 100 yards (about 91 m) of a cultural or historical site or structure, over occupied beaches, campgrounds, restrooms or equestrian facilities, or over the viewing platforms at Tahquamenon Falls and Palms Book. Commercial drone use also needs prior written department permission.

Michigan prohibits possessing or consuming alcohol throughout Belle Isle, Grand Haven, Holland and several other named state parks, subject to possible written event permission. Other parks have seasonal or area-specific restrictions; check the department list for the precise park.
Michigan state parks and recreation areas require a Recreation Passport for vehicle entry; the department says entry on foot or by non-motorised bicycle is free.

At Michigan state parks, Roman candles and bottle rockets are prohibited; the department lists smaller novelty items such as sparklers and ground spinners as permitted. Check any additional local fire restrictions.

In Michigan state parks pets must be under immediate control and leashed on a lead no longer than 6 feet (about 1.8 m), with exceptions for dogs in lawful hunting or training on open land. Pets cannot be left unattended; beaches, buildings and some other areas have restrictions. Service animals are exempt from the building restrictions.
